title: Mg₂Fe₂O₅ Nanoparticle-Decorated Ca₂Fe₂O₅−CaFe₂O₄ Heterostructure for Efficient Photocatalytic CO₂ Conversion
soWhat: Used DFT to pin down where CO₂ and water turn into hydrocarbons on a Ca₂Fe₂O₅−CaFe₂O₄ heterostructure, and how the charge separation works.
problem: The heterostructure contains several metal sites. Once the experiments showed improved activity, it was still unclear which site actually drives the reduction and how the Type-II band alignment suppresses charge recombination.
role: Second author. I was responsible for the simulation work; material synthesis and photocatalytic measurements were done by the other authors.
method: The calculations show that the formaldehyde pathway at the Fe site of Ca₂Fe₂O₅ (001) converts CO₂ into CH₄ and is the preferred active site. The band diagram matches Type-II charge transfer: electrons stay on Ca₂Fe₂O₅ for the reduction while holes move to CaFe₂O₄ for water oxidation.
